$comment: U47's deferred item: the telltale cathode escape vias sit with their CENTRE
inside the LED pad. Same net, so DRC never says a word -- but at reflow
solder wicks down the barrel, and the estimate on record is up to ~22% of a
pad's deposit, giving an asymmetric fillet and a tilted LED behind a lens.
It was deferred because it looked like a coordinated two-layer re-route,
four times, in the densest part of the board.
Three of the four are not that. Every one is the same shape -- a via at the
pad centre, a short stub to the pad, and a longer track running away -- so
the fix is to slide the via out along the direction its track ALREADY runs
and lengthen the stub. No net changes layer, no topology is re-established.
LED2 is the exception and is NOT in this file. /U12_RSTN hems it in on every
side: the best position anywhere around the pad clears by 0.133, and routing
east under the pad (legal -- the pad is top-only) fails because /U12_RSTN
crosses beneath it, -0.034 at x=235.5. Closing LED2 means moving /U12_RSTN,
which is a separate decision on a net already documented as running at
Clearances at the new via centres, against the 0.1016 rule:

steps.step: 1/3  LED6 -- slide the via south, the way its Bottom track already runs
2/3  LED7 -- slide the via south; its feed is on Inner1, not Bottom
3/3  LED8 -- slide the via west, the way its Bottom track already runs
